subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw's native backup CLI add gitignore-style exclusions now, and what defaults/protected-path rules are acceptable for restore-critical and sensitive data?
rationale: The request changes a core recovery/security command, and the active PR leaves unresolved choices around auto-loaded ignore files, external assets, protected paths, dependency surface, and proof that automation should not choose for maintainers.

options.title: Narrow and review the native PR
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask maintainers to narrow https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 into an opt-in, proof-backed design with explicit protected restore paths and no silent backup-scope changes.

options.title: Defer native excludes
options.body: Keep this as a product backlog item and direct users to Keep My Claw or manual cleanup until maintainers are ready to own the core CLI surface.

options.title: Reject native scope
options.body: Close the core request only after documenting the supported plugin or ClawHub alternative and its security tradeoffs.

recommendation.title: Narrow and review the native PR
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and ask maintainers to narrow https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 into an opt-in, proof-backed design with explicit protected restore paths and no silent backup-scope changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The initial backup CLI merge and archive-boundary refactor make this the strongest available routing signal for the product/security decision, with shichangs and brettdavies as useful context owners.
